overall: Atlanta is tracking a warming afternoon with current conditions at 80.6°F as of 12:20 ET, still gaining heat at +3.6°F/hr. The morning was notably suppressed by overcast skies (OVC/100% cloud cover from ~05:52 through 10:52 ET), but a partial clearing to BKN (~62% cloud fraction) around midday unleashed rapid warming — temps jumped roughly 7-8°F in the 11:00–12:20 window. The NWS forecast calls for a high near 88°F with mostly sunny skies and only a slight storm chance after 5 PM, suggesting no convective ceiling on afternoon heating.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in moderate agreement but running cooler than NWS narrative: ECMWF at 85.5°F, HRRR at 83.9°F, and NBM at 86.2°F average to roughly 85°F, well below the 88°F NWS point forecast. The late-morning cloud lid likely caused models to underperform in the morning, but with skies now partially clearing and 2+ hours of insolation remaining before the projected ~14:42 ET peak, observed temps are on pace to challenge the mid-to-upper 80s. The ensemble signals flag high uncertainty (Tier 4, no-trade) with disagreement across sub-models.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 80.6°F at 12:20 ET, a projected peak near 14.7h, and current warming velocity of +3.6°F/hr (decelerating as solar angle falls and BKN cloud cover limits insolation), an additional 5-7°F of warming is plausible, pointing to a daily high in the 85-87°F range. The META model concentrates roughly 54% probability in the 84-89°F band (split between 84-85F and 86-87F at 26.9% each), broadly consistent with the INTRADAY model's peak at 84-85°F (37.5%). The NWS 88°F target is achievable only if skies clear further and warming maintains above-average efficiency; confidence is moderate with a central estimate near 86°F.
